newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Uneasy calm in Tirana, evacuations under way.
newsitem.headline: Uneasy calm in Tirana, evacuations under way.

text.p: Italian military helicopters lifted foreigners at dawn on Friday from a Tirana soccer stadium as an uneasy calm settled over the city after a night in which Albanian rebels fired looted guns wildly into the air.

In Rome, the Italian foreign ministry said it had completed an operation to evacuate around 1,000 foreign nationals and some locals from Albania in an air and sea operation that began on Thursday afternoon and was coordinated by Italy's ambassador in Tirana.
Officials at a military hospital in the Albanian capital said a total of three people, including a four-year-old girl and a 10-year-old boy, were killed and 72 injured by stray bullets.

European mediator Franz Vranitzky, meanwhile, planned to meet Albanian government ministers on Friday aboard an Italian warship off the country's Adriatic coast, a spokeswoman for the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) said.

In New York, the United Nations Security Council late on Thursday issued a statement appealing to Albanians "to refrain from hostilities and acts of violence and to cooperate with diplomatic efforts to reach a peaceful solution to the crisis".

Several big Italian twin-rotor Chinook cargo helicopters landed in the centre of the soccer pitch as several dozen evacuees, apparently Westerners and most carrying one or two small suitcases, lined up to board them. The stadium is close to government buildings and the U.S. embassy.
Tanks were absent from the streets of the Albanian capital on Friday morning. They had been sent out late on Thursday to help stem the virtual anarchy gripping Albania.
Most shops in the city were closed but some cafes opened. Road traffic was about half the normal flow in the city centre.
At the stadium, a small number of Italian troops deployed during the dawn airlift. Italian officials on the spot refused to comment on the evacuation to reporters.

In London, the British Foreign Office said it had evacuated 131 people successfully from Albania by on Friday morning and they were now on their way to the Italian Adriatic port of Brindisi aboard an Italian naval vessel.

A foreign office spokesman said the 131, including 65 Britons, three Irish citizens, 11 Commonwealth citizens and 52 others, had been safely taken off the beach in the port of Durres, about 30 km (20 miles) west of Tirana.
The Austrian embassy in Tirana said about 100 evacuees, including Greeks and Austrians, were waiting for transport to Durres.

The OSCE spokeswoman, speaking to reporters by telephone, said Vranitzky had flown from Vienna to Brindisi and was about to go by helicopter to the ship. Senior Albanian officials, including newly appointed Prime Minister Bashkim Fino, were waiting on the vessel. President Sali Berisha, she said, was not in attendance.
Vranitzky held talks last week with Berisha in Tirana and had urged him to avoid violence in dealing with the rebellion. A top-level European Union mission also came to Tirana.
He had planned to return to the Albanian capital on Thursday but was prevented from travelling by the deterioriating security situation and the closure of Tirana airport.
Berisha and Albania's new all-party government have appealed to Europe's NATO members for military help to restore order.
The mounting lawlessness in Albania has occurred often with demoralised soldiers watching and making no attempt to halt it.
Albania's chaotic revolt, which began in the south where people have lost their savings in collapsed pyramid investment schemes, has spread to the north of the country since mid-week.

As pressure mounted on Berisha from the rebels who want him to resign before they will consider handing back the arms they have stolen, two of his children fled to Italy by ferry with two armed bodyguards.

Albania's government called for foreign military intervention to halt the disorder, but German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said the crisis was essentially an internal matter and it was not clear what foreign troops would do there.

On Thursday, the United States sent four Chinook military helicopters into Tirana to pull out its citizens. About 50 Americans, most of them children, had already been ferried out of the country to U.S. ships standing offshore, the State Department said.
